who is a dog

A dog is a domesticated animal that originated from wolves in central Asia and has been a companion to humans for at least 13,000 years. They are carnivorous or omnivorous, and there are around 340 different breeds of dogs, ranging from the largest to the smallest, all descended from the same wolf ancestors. Dogs are known for their strong bonds with humans, earning them the nickname "man's best friend."

dog

Dogs originated in central Asia and have been companions to humans as far back as 13,000 BC. They were initially wolves that were run off of camps, but people later realized that it was cleaner to have them around because they ate garbage and rats. Dogs also served as an alarm system, barking when something was approaching. 

Some fun facts about dogs include: 
- They have a highly developed sense of smell, able to differentiate smells that are lower than 1 million times that which a human can.
- They can hear sounds that are four times the distance away than a human can.
- The average lifespan of a dog is 10 to 14 years.
- Dogs tend to have more than one puppy at a time, and those puppies are called a litter.
- There are approximately 400 million dogs on the planet.
- Dogs have formed strong bonds with humans, earning them the nickname "man's best friend."
